era_note: Port Valdez and Prince William Sound, 24 March 1989, and the safety record that followed. Per episode_spec forbidden_claims, no Short states a probable cause for the grounding (NTSB/MAR-90/04 is an unread scan), says the master was drunk at the wheel or was steering (the vessel was under the third mate's navigational control), says the third mate was negligent or asleep, says Exxon was uniquely bad among tanker operators (the Board records the chief-mate practice as widely practised), gives any oil figure other than about 258,000 barrels, says the Supreme Court let Exxon off, or says the accident happened because one man left the bridge. Per forbidden_subjects, nothing about oiled wildlife, dead animals or shoreline carcasses - the imagery that has always buried the manning finding.

Subjects from the episode's own Codex plate table: the bunk and the cabin V001/V021-V026, the cargo operation V013-V020/V055, the bridge and the lookout V007-V012/V031-V036, the watch bill V005/V047-V050, the Sound V037-V041. shorts.angle: Every ship carries a number: the smallest crew it may sail with. This one was worked out for a run to Panama. The run changed to California - weeks at sea became days - and the number never moved.
shorts.avoids: Names nobody, states no probable cause, and says nothing about the master or alcohol. Does not say Exxon was uniquely bad - the Board's own note that the practice is widely used belongs to the second Short and is not contradicted here.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: If the crew was set for a longer voyage, what was the first thing that got dropped on the short one?
shorts.loop_join: The close - the vessel usually put to sea with a fatigued crew - answers the hook's question about what a crew number promises.

lines.text: There is a number written on a piece of paper for every ship at sea. It is the smallest number of people the ship is allowed to sail with.
source_lines: There is a number written on a piece of paper for every ship at sea.
It is the smallest number of people the ship is allowed to sail with.

lines.text: It is set once, against how the ship is expected to be used. It is a document. It sits in a file.
source_lines: It is set once, for a ship, against how she is expected to be used.
It is a document.
It sits in a file.

lines.text: And it does not follow the ship around asking whether anything changed.
source_lines: And it does not follow the ship around asking whether anything has changed.

lines.text: When the minimum crew requirements were established, the vessel had been scheduled for the Valdez-to-Panama trade. Weeks at sea. Time for the watch system to settle, time for people to sleep.
source_lines: When the minimum crew requirements were established for the EXXON VALDEZ, the vessel had been scheduled for the Valdez-to-Panama trade.
Weeks at sea.
Time for maintenance, time for the watch system to settle into three watches, time for people to sleep.

lines.text: That trade was discontinued after December 1988. The ship began operating regularly between Valdez and ports in California. A much shorter passage. The same number of people.
source_lines: That trade was discontinued after December 1988.
And the ship began operating regularly between Valdez and ports in California.
A much shorter passage.
The same number of people.

lines.text: Union officials testified that the passages between Alaska and California were not long enough for necessary maintenance, or for thorough crew rest.
source_lines: The Board records what the union officials testified about that: the sea passages between Alaska and California were not long enough for necessary maintenance, or for thorough crew rest, between the around-the-clock demands of cargo handling in port.

lines.text: The mates on the EXXON VALDEZ were usually fatigued after cargo handling operations in Valdez, and the vessel usually put to sea with a fatigued crew.
source_lines: "The mates on the EXXON VALDEZ were usually fatigued after cargo handling operations in Valdez, and the vessel usually put to sea with a fatigued crew."

lines.text: Usually. Both times. The number on the paper had not moved.
source_lines: Usually.
Both times.
The number had not moved.

shorts.angle: A lookout is a person whose whole job is to look at the water and say what is on it. On this ship the position routinely went unattended - because taking it away costs nothing, almost every time.
shorts.avoids: Blames no crew member; the Board's word routinely is quoted as its own. Does not state a probable cause and does not say the grounding was caused by the lookout being away. Says nothing about the master or alcohol.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: The company had its own rule about two officers on the bridge. What did the Board say about relying on it?
shorts.loop_join: The close - which is exactly why it is the first thing that gets taken away - returns to the hook's job of being the only other pair of eyes.

lines.text: The EXXON VALDEZ was operated with a reduced crew complement, and the Board states that watchkeeping safeguards had been compromised because of the manning level.
source_lines: The EXXON VALDEZ was operated with a reduced crew complement, and the Board states that evidence indicated watchkeeping safeguards had been compromised because of the manning level.

lines.text: There were not enough unlicensed crew on deck to keep an uninterrupted lookout when other routine duties came up.
source_lines: There were not enough unlicensed crew in the deck department to keep an uninterrupted lookout when other routine duties came up.

lines.text: When one able seaman had to take the helm, the remaining hands had to cover all the work and the lookout, unless somebody was called in on overtime.
source_lines: When one able seaman had to take the helm, the remaining hands had to cover all the work and the lookout, unless somebody was called in from another watch on overtime.

lines.text: As a result, on the EXXON VALDEZ, the lookout position routinely went unattended when the AB was called for other tasks or took a break.
source_lines: "As a result, on the EXXON VALDEZ, the lookout position routinely went unattended when the AB was called for other tasks or took a break."

lines.text: Routinely. Not once.
source_lines: Routinely.
Not once.

lines.text: And notice what a lookout is for. It is not a formality and it is not a second opinion.
source_lines: And notice what a lookout is for.
It is not a formality and it is not a second opinion.

lines.text: It is a person whose entire job is to look at the water and say what is on it, so the officer conning the ship is not the only pair of eyes in the dark.
source_lines: It is a person whose entire job is to look at the water and say what is on it, so that the officer conning the ship does not have to be the only pair of eyes in the dark.

lines.text: Take that person away for twenty minutes and nothing happens, almost every time. Which is exactly why it is the first thing that gets taken away.
source_lines: Take that person away for twenty minutes and nothing happens, almost every time.
Which is exactly why it is the first thing that gets taken away.

kinetic_beats.anchor: the first thing that gets taken away

shorts.angle: The Board listed four things it could find no reasonable explanation for. The third: a crewmember's performance rated partly on willingness to work overtime. The fourth: the workloads went up after the grounding.
shorts.avoids: States the Board's word foreseeable with the Board's own meaning - the category of accident was visible from where the decision was made, not that anyone predicted this grounding. Does not say Exxon was uniquely bad, does not state a probable cause, says nothing about the master.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Nineteen years later a second institution found the same shape from different evidence. What did it write down?
shorts.loop_join: The close - the workloads went up after - is the fourth item the hook promised, landing hardest.

lines.text: The Board's verdict: the reduced manning practices of the company are generally incautious and without apparent justification from the standpoint of safety.
source_lines: The reduced manning practices of the company are "generally incautious and without apparent justification from the standpoint of safety.

lines.text: And the financial advantage of taking officers and crew off each vessel does not seem to justify incurring the foreseeable risks of serious accidents.
source_lines: And the financial advantage of taking officers and crew off each vessel "does not seem to justify incurring the foreseeable risks of serious accidents."

lines.text: Foreseeable. It does not mean somebody predicted this night. It means the category of accident was visible from where the decision was made.
source_lines: Foreseeable.
It does not mean somebody predicted this grounding.
It means the category of accident was visible from where the decision was made.

lines.text: A company deciding how many people to put on a ship is not asked to see the future. It is asked to look at a schedule and a workload, and work out whether the people can stay awake.
source_lines: A company deciding how many people to put on a ship is not being asked to see the future.
It is being asked to look at a schedule, a watch system and a workload, and to work out whether the people in it can stay awake.

lines.text: Finally, the Board lists four things for which it found no reasonable explanation.
source_lines: Finally, the Board lists four things for which it could find no reasonable explanation.

lines.text: The practice of rating a crewmember's performance in part according to willingness to work overtime.
source_lines: The practice of rating a crewmember's performance in part according to willingness to work overtime — giving an incentive to work an excessive number of hours.

lines.text: The appraisal that decides your promotion, your pay and your next ship, partly measured by how willing you are to be tired.
source_lines: The appraisal that decides your promotion, your pay and your next ship, partly measured by how willing you are to be tired.

lines.text: And the fourth: the indiscriminate increase in work loads throughout the fleet, before and after. After. The workloads went up after this happened.
source_lines: The indiscriminate increase in work loads and standby time throughout the fleet, before and after the grounding.
After.
The workloads went up after this happened.
